topics.title: Asia trip puts nuclear talks in view
topics.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump began an Asia trip featuring ASEAN meetings and planned talks with China and Russia, where Ukraine and nuclear arms are expected to be discussed.
topics.discussionPrompt: When leaders plan a big meeting, what makes you hopeful it will be useful: a clear agenda, smaller side conversations, or simply everyone showing up?

topics.title: UN offers support for nuclear reductions
topics.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres said the United Nations is ready to support any denuclearisation effort that emerges from this week's U.S., China and Russia summit.
topics.discussionPrompt: Big international goals can feel abstract. What small sign would convince you that a peace-focused agreement was actually moving from words into action?

topics.title: AI chip rules tighten before summit
topics.summary: The U.S. issued rules restricting remote access to advanced AI chips and servers, a move expected to be part of wider technology discussions with China this week.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a powerful new technology needs rules, should the first rules focus on access, safety testing, or who is accountable when something goes wrong?

topics.title: AI safety stays on the agenda
topics.summary: U.S. and Chinese officials are expected to discuss AI-safety cooperation at the Shenzhen summit, even as disagreements over advanced-chip access remain a major issue.
topics.discussionPrompt: Two rivals can still agree on safety rails. What everyday situation works better when competitors cooperate on a shared rule?

topics.title: COP31 draft opens climate bargaining
topics.summary: COP31 negotiators released a draft agreement in Turkey, beginning a push to narrow differences over fossil fuels, climate finance and how countries respond to rising temperatures.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a group has to agree on a difficult plan, is it better to start with a huge messy draft or a short list of things everyone already shares?

topics.title: An early polar-vortex wobble
topics.summary: Meteorologists say the Arctic polar vortex is weakening unusually early. It does not guarantee a harsh winter, but it can raise the chance of colder, drier conditions in some northern regions.
topics.discussionPrompt: What is your ideal cold-weather routine: cooking something warm, finding a favorite show, getting outdoors, or making the home extra cozy?

topics.title: U.S. flights work toward normal
topics.summary: U.S. air travel continued recovering after a nationwide ground stop disrupted flights. Officials said aging systems and problems during technology work were being investigated.
topics.discussionPrompt: Travel plans go sideways sometimes. Are you the person who makes a backup plan immediately, or the one who finds an unexpected adventure?

topics.title: AI stocks face another wobbly day
topics.summary: U.S. markets fell as AI-related shares, led by Nvidia, declined again. Investors are watching the sector closely ahead of Nvidia's upcoming earnings report.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a popular trend suddenly cools off, do you get more curious about what changed, or do you prefer to wait and see where things settle?

topics.title: Vikings win a key division game
topics.summary: Minnesota beat Green Bay 30-10 after forcing four turnovers and recording eight sacks, tightening a three-way race at the top of the NFC North.
topics.discussionPrompt: What makes a team win feel especially satisfying: a comeback, smart defense, an old favorite returning, or a perfectly executed plan?

topics.title: London City earns a point at Arsenal
topics.summary: London City Lionesses drew 1-1 at Arsenal in the Women's Super League, with goalkeeper Mary Earps making key saves to help preserve third place.
topics.discussionPrompt: A great save can matter as much as a great goal. Which kind of effort do you notice most: a dramatic finish, quiet consistency, or helping someone else shine?
